subject: Post-demo: Acme model shortlist and next steps (follow-up)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.j@acme.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 16:15:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: Acme model shortlist and next steps

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for taking the time today — really appreciated the overview of Acme's search summarization use case and the constraints you called out (p95 latency target ~200ms, budget target ~$0.01 / inference on your typical 200-token average, and strict PII retention rules). As promised, below is a short, prioritized model shortlist with rationale and recommended next steps for evaluation. I kept tradeoffs explicit so we can pick the right route for the first pilot.

Quick recap of goals from the call:
- Real-time summarization for search snippets (p95 latency <= 200ms)
- Production cost goal: ~<$0.01 per inference on average workload
- High semantic fidelity on legal/financial language (strong quality requirement)
- No customer data persisted beyond session; enterprise-grade auditability required

Recommended shortlist (ranked):
1) Redwood-2.0-base-quant (recommended pilot)
   - Rationale: best balance of quality and latency on our Dedicated and Hosted stacks. Quantized to 4-bit which reduces GPU memory and cost while keeping quality within 2-3% of full fp16 on our internal ROUGE/BLEU-style metrics for your promptset.
   - Expected perf: ~120-160ms p95 on standard A10G-backed Dedicated pod for 200-token avg; cost projection ~ $0.008 - $0.012 / inference depending on batching.

2) Llama-3-13B-q4
   - Rationale: lower-cost option, good semantic coherence on short summaries; slightly lower hallucination robustness on niche legal terms.
   - Expected perf: ~90-140ms p95 (lower compute footprint) but quality drop vs Redwood-2.0 on edge cases. Cost projection ~ $0.006 - $0.009 / inference.

3) Llama-3-70B-fp16 (quality-first)
   - Rationale: highest quality for nuanced legal/financial text and lowest regression risk, but significantly higher cost and latency. Good fallback for high-value queries where correctness is critical.
   - Expected perf: ~350-500ms p95 on same pod (unless scaled to higher tier GPUs); cost projection ~ $0.03+ / inference.

Notes on tradeoffs and mitigations:
- Caching & prefix KV caching: many of your queries are repetitive; enabling prefix caching reduces effective cost and p95 for Redwood-2.0 and Llama-3-13B significantly. We can include a cache policy in the pilot.
- Batching: small dynamic batching (20-50ms wait window) improves throughput and reduces cost but will increase median latency slightly — we can tune per-route.
- Quality/regression: we recommend a prompt-based eval harness (we already prepared a 500-prompt set — attached as acme_prompt_set_v1.csv) and continuous evals against a small holdout. We’ll configure alerts for regressions >3% on your primary metrics and automatic rollback to the previous model version if triggered.

Attachments: redwood_model_shortlist_summary.pdf (summary + cost calc), acme_prompt_set_v1.csv (500 prompts)
Benchmarks and detailed numbers: https://drive.google.com/redwood/acme/model-benchmarks-2026

Proposed next steps:
- Your team: confirm which 2 models you want in the pilot (recommended: Redwood-2.0-base-quant + Llama-3-13B-q4)
- Redwood: spin a 7-day canary with both models behind a feature flag, run the 500-prompt eval + a live traffic canary for 24-72 hours, share detailed per-route p95 and cost breakdowns
- Schedule: suggest a 60-min technical run-of-show next week to align on rollout and SLOs (I’m available Tue/Wed afternoon PT).

If you want, Rishi and Dev are on this thread and can handle the test run setup / access.

Thanks — happy to walk through the attached summary live.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Post-demo: Acme model shortlist and next steps

Great questions — answers below. I've also included a short checklist for the pilot setup.

1) Redwood-2.0-base-quant numbers: the ~120-160ms p95 quoted is uncached, single-request p95 on our Dedicated A10G pod with default batching (no artificial wait window). With prefix caching enabled for repeated queries we typically see effective p95 drop to ~80-110ms for your traffic profile. We will provide both cached/uncached distributions in the benchmark report.

2) Cost projections: the numbers I shared are for Dedicated (including compute and orchestration) but exclude network egress. Hosted runs have slightly higher per-inference CPU overhead and can increase cost by ~10-15% depending on volume and egress. For spikes, we recommend reserve capacity with burst policies (Redwood Dedicated) to control unit price during end-of-month spikes. We can model a 99th percentile spike simulation for you during the pilot.

Prompt categories included in acme_prompt_set_v1.csv (high-level):
- Search intent summaries (short/medium/long) — 220 prompts
- Legal / compliance language extraction — 80 prompts
- Numeric / financial extraction checks — 60 prompts
- Edge-case noisy queries (OCR errors, mixed languages) — 70 prompts

Pilot setup checklist (what we'll do on our side):
- Provision two model endpoints (Redwood-2.0-base-quant, Llama-3-13B-q4) on a Dedicated pod
- Run offline evals across the 500 prompts and provide per-prompt scores + aggregated metrics (ROUGE-like, factuality heuristic)
- Run a 24-72h live canary routing 5-10% of traffic to the canary models with traffic shadowing for the rest
- Produce a cost/latency breakdown (per-route and token-level) and regression alerts config

Canary KPIs we recommend:
- p95 latency delta vs baseline < +50ms for Redwood-2.0; < +30ms for Llama-3-13B (if you choose to prioritize lower latency)
- Quality delta: <3% drop on primary intent accuracy metric or automatic rollback
- Error rate <0.5% (timeouts, 5xx errors)

I've attached the benchmark summary and the prompt set. The Drive link has a full runbook and the scripts we'll use to reproduce numbers: https://drive.google.com/redwood/acme/model-benchmarks-2026

Wed 1:00pm PT works for Rishi and me — please send a calendar invite and we’ll add Dev to handle provisioning.

Best,
Marissa
